case_title: Deepak Kumar Shrivas & Anr. v. State of Chhattisgarh & Ors.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior financial dealing: money paid by respondent no.6 to the appellant for a job for her daughter; no family or personal relationship stated
evidence_type: Documentary and testimonial material from preliminary police enquiry (recorded statements, enquiry report); FIR allegation of cash payment with no bank transactions
high_court_outcome: Writ petition under Article 226 for quashing FIR and proceedings dismissed
neutral_facts: The victim alleged that the accused and his brother took about Rs 4 lakh in cash in April 2019 on the promise of securing a job for the victim's daughter in a government department or the private sector, to be provided within three months. According to the FIR, no job was provided and the payment was made entirely in cash with no bank transactions. Earlier, in 2021, the other party had complained to the district Collector that the victim had demanded money for securing a job for the accused's brother and had paid about Rs 80,000 cash plus further bank deposits. The complaint was referred to the police for enquiry. The Station House Officer recorded statements from both parties and other persons. In that enquiry the victim stated that Rs 4 lakh had been paid for the daughter's job. Both sides alleged that false complaints were being made against each other. The enquiry noted that the parties did not produce the documents, call records or recorded conversations sought, and it recommended closing that complaint. Later, on 27 July 2022, the victim lodged an FIR against the accused and his brother. Before registration, a further enquiry found that both parties had made allegations against each other of taking money for providing jobs.
financial_property_loss: Per appellant's complaint: Rs 80,000 cash plus about Rs 20,000 deposited in bank accounts; per FIR allegation: Rs 4 lakh paid in cash in April 2019
motive: Court accepted: FIR lodged to recover money under coercion and pressure, not for prosecution of an offence
key_evidence_accepted: Recorded statement of respondent no.6 in the earlier enquiry that she paid Rs 4 lakh for her daughter's job; the record of the earlier enquiry
witness_credibility: Court found the parties' conduct and claims prima facie tainted with suspicion; the complainant's unexplained delay raised doubts on the authenticity of the claims
trial_duration: offence: April 2019 (alleged payment); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 11.07.2023; Supreme Court: 19.02.2024
legal_representation: Appellants: Sameer Shrivastava, Dr. Sangeeta Verma, Shivendra Dixit. Respondents (including State counsel, not separately identified): Gautam Narayan, Ms. Asmita Singh, Harshit Goel, Sujay Jain, Sachin Patil, Kailas Bajirao Autade, Sunil Kumar Sethi
investigation_status: FIR registered as Crime No. 248 of 2022 on 27.07.2022 after earlier preliminary enquiries; the proceedings arising from it were quashed by the Supreme Court
procedural_irregularity: Court noted an unexplained delay of about three years in lodging the FIR; no other procedural lapse noted
appeal_history: Trial court: Not stated (FIR stage). High Court: writ petition under Article 226 dismissed on 11.07.2023. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, proceedings arising out of FIR 248 of 2022 quashed
prosecution_argument: A cognizable offence was disclosed; investigation should continue and the appellant can challenge the charge sheet and seek discharge later; it was a clear case of cheating
defence_argument: Earlier enquiry on similar mutual allegations was not substantiated; FIR is a mala fide counterblast to recover money; the FIR is barred by delay of more than three years
legal_principle_applied: Criminal proceedings may be quashed where the FIR's object is recovery of money under coercion rather than prosecution, considering unexplained delay, prior inquiry and abuse of process; police must exercise heightened caution in such disputes
other_sentence_order: Impugned High Court order set aside and all proceedings arising out of FIR No. 248 of 2022 quashed. Court also made general suggestions to police to exercise heightened caution (para 15)
